web_evidence.title: The Presence of Africanisms and the Representation of Blackness in Contemporary North American Literature Written by White Women
web_evidence.note: University-hosted scholarly analysis states that Skeeter, Aibileen, and Minny narrate in first person and that Chapter XXV, The Benefit, is instead told by an omniscient narrator, establishing sustained first- and third-person sections.

web_evidence.title: A-Level English Literature (AQA) – The Help
web_evidence.note: The educational analysis explicitly describes the novel's rotation among three first-person narrators and identifies Chapter 25, The Benefit, as a shift to third-person narration.

web_evidence.title: The Help Chapter 25 Summary
web_evidence.note: The chapter guide identifies The Benefit as the sole chapter narrated by an unnamed third-person narrator; this is component evidence for the exceptional section, not independently sufficient whole-book ALTERNATING support.

web_evidence.title: A Teacher's Guide to The Help by Kathryn Stockett
web_evidence.note: Penguin's teacher guide treats Chapter 25, The Benefit, as narrationally different from the rest of the novel, corroborating that the chapter is structurally exceptional without itself naming both grammatical persons.

person_note: The quotes repeatedly and unmistakably expose participating first-person narration by the novel's character narrators, but the popularity-selected sample contains no passage from the exceptional Chapter 25. Web research resolves the structure: most chapters are narrated in first person by Aibileen, Minny, or Skeeter, while the sustained chapter The Benefit uses an unnamed omniscient third-person narrator. Under the methodology, that cross-person chapter structure is ALTERNATING even though first person overwhelmingly predominates. Confidence is med because quote evidence supports only the first-person component and only one Tier A/B source directly supports the complete ALTERNATING structure; the second exact whole-book source is Tier C, so the required two-Tier-A/B threshold for high confidence is not met. Audit: independent review confirmed the three sustained first-person narrators and the exceptional third-person Chapter 25; the ALTERNATING/med decision and source tiers are retained.
